hypotheses.note: x : ℤ, 0 < n, T^[n] x = x for the refutations, the identities and the bound. The conditional theorem (theo_syracuse_cycle_of_cited) also assumes x > 0 and n the least period (strengthened). Without either one the statement is false (findings 1, 2).
Read as a_i(x_0): α : ℤ → ℕ n-periodic with α k = a_k(x), as in the strict UpperBounds.

Both conventions: α k = a_k(x) and β (k+1) = a_k(x). The count over ⟦1, n⟧ is shift-invariant (twoDescCount_shift), so the statement is the same in both (theo_syracuse_cycle_printed_false (ii), theo_syracuse_cycle_of_cited_shift).
Read as 𝒟_Γ = … (TwoDescClasses). For periodic a it is equivalent to #(𝒟 ∩ ⟦1, n⟧) = 2 with 1 ≤ k₁ < k₂ ≤ n (twoDescCount_eq_two_iff).

hypotheses.paper: an ascending index in each gap (implicit in l.308; the case k₂ = k₁ + 1 is set aside at l.328)

hypotheses.paper: the corollary to Matveev's theorem; the computer check (l.326)
hypotheses.note: Cited results, carried as explicit hypotheses: TwoDescMatveev B (effective, at ε₀ and constant 2) and TwoDescCheck B (no positive cycle of least period n with p_n ≤ B has two descending indices). Never axioms. They are T-syr-cited's question.

findings: syracuse.tex:306 — false over ℤ. The cycle −17 → −25 → −37 → −55 → −41 → −61 → −91 has least period 7 (Syracuse.twoDesc_neg_seventeen_minimal) and a = (1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 4). So 𝒟 ∩ ⟦1, 7⟧ = {3, 6}, and {4, 7} in the other index convention (twoDescCount_seq17, theo_syracuse_cycle_printed_false). This bears on OQ-63 (a), the sign of the cycles, and decides nothing.

syracuse.tex:306 — with n any period, the statement fails also for x > 0. The cycle (1) read as a 2-cycle has a ≡ 2 and 𝒟 ∩ ⟦1, 2⟧ = {1, 2} (theo_syracuse_cycle_nonminimal_false). The statement needs n to be the least period.

syracuse.tex:308 — '#𝒟_Γ = (k₁ + nℤ) ∪ (k₂ + nℤ)' equates a number with a set. Read as 𝒟_Γ = …, it is equivalent, for periodic a, to the theorem's #(𝒟 ∩ ⟦1, n⟧) = 2 with 1 ≤ k₁ < k₂ ≤ n (twoDescCount_eq_two_iff). This confirms the planner's [r] (b).

syracuse.tex:310–315 — the exact displays are false for both readings of OQ-43 and both readings of the positions. The true two-term form at an ascending u is twoDesc_deltaAlt_two_terms (twoDesc_delta_two_terms for the printed A_u^n). Its exponents are s₁ − 1 and s₂ − 2 + a, where the displays have s₁ and s₂ − 1 + a: the error of lem:syracuse_cycle_n__n_, OQ-68 (b). The display of l.311–312 has the shape for k₂ − n < u < k₁, the positions l.308 gives to j, and there it is 2Δ'_u = (2/3)Δ_u (twoDesc_displayI_eq). Symmetrically, l.313–314 is 2Δ'_u for k₁ < u < k₂, the positions of i (twoDesc_displayJ_eq). This confirms the planner's [r] (a), up to the factor 2. At the printed positions the exponent k₁ − i is negative. At −17 neither display equals Δ'_u or Δ_u at any ascending u of a period (twoDesc_displays_printed_false).

syracuse.tex:317–322 — both ∼_S forms are false as printed. The true forms at the positions of l.308 are as follows. For k₁ < i < k₂, Δ'_i = 3^{i−k₁−1} 2^{k₂−i} E(δ₂, α₂, α₁) and Δ_i = 3^{i−k₁} 2^{k₂−i} E(δ₂, α₂, α₁) (twoDesc_delta_i). For k₂ − n < j < k₁, Δ_j = 3^{j+n−k₂} 2^{k₁−j} E(δ₁, α₁, α₂) (twoDesc_delta_j). Here E(δ, α, β) = 3^δ(2^α − 1) + 2^{δ+α}(2^β − 1). So Δ_i ∼_S 3^{δ₂}(2^{α₂} − 1) + 2^{δ₂+α₂}(2^{α₁} − 1): l.318's δ₂ with α₁ and α₂ exchanged, as the planner's [r] (a) says. The same exchange holds for l.320. Equivalently, l.318 and l.320 are what the displays of l.310–315 give with δ₁ and δ₂ exchanged. At −17 (k₁ = 3, k₂ = 6, δ₁ = 3, δ₂ = 4, α₁ = 1, α₂ = 3), the true S-free parts are 139 and 695 = 5·139. The printed ones are 305 = 5·61 and 253 = 11·23. No Δ_u, u ∈ ℤ, is ∼_S to either printed one, under both readings of OQ-43 (twoDesc_values_seq17, twoDesc_sEquiv_printed_false).

syracuse.tex:323–324 — the WLOG is not needed. 2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ divides both E(δ₁, α₁, α₂) and E(δ₂, α₂, α₁), so m = |2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ| is at most each (twoDesc_abs_le). Hence m ≤ 2^{|Γ|−n}(3^δ + 2^δ) with δ = min(δ₁, δ₂) ≤ n/2 (twoDesc_bound), and in real form m ≤ 3^{n/2}2^{|Γ|−n} + 2^{|Γ|−n}2^{n/2} (twoDesc_bound_rpow). Read literally on Δ_j, the first inequality of l.324 is false: at −17 every ascending u has Δ'_u ≥ 1112 > 3^{7/2}·2⁴ + 2⁴·2^{7/2} (twoDesc_l324_first_literal_false). It holds for the S-free part.

syracuse.tex:324–325 — the second inequality, 3^{n/2}2^{|Γ|−n} + 2^{|Γ|−n}2^{n/2} ≤ 2^{|Γ|−(log₃2 − 1/2)|Γ|}, is false whenever 3ⁿ < 2^{|Γ|}, so on every cycle of x > 0 (twoDesc_l324_second_false, twoDesc_l324_second_printed_false). It needs n ≥ |Γ| log₃ 2, the reverse of 2^{p_n} > 3ⁿ. What holds: p_n ≤ 2n on every cycle of ℤ (twoDesc_p_le), so (2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ)⁴ ≤ 16·12^{p_n} (twoDesc_bound_pow_four). That is, m ≤ 2·2^{|Γ|(1−ε₀)} with ε₀ = 1/2 − (log₂ 3)/4 ≈ 0.104 > 0, on every cycle of ℤ with two descending indices per period (twoDesc_corollary_hyp). This is the hypothesis of cor:property_defined_cycles_gcd, with ε₀ in place of log₃ 2 − 1/2.

syracuse.tex:326 — the corollary to Matveev's theorem and the computer check are cited, not proved. Carried as the hypotheses TwoDescMatveev B and TwoDescCheck B, they give the statement for x > 0 and n the least period (theo_syracuse_cycle_of_cited; _shift for the other index convention).

syracuse.tex:328 — the case k₂ = k₁ + 1 is not a separate case. The key identity A'_{k₂+1} + (2^P − 3ⁿ) = 2^{δ₂}E(δ₁, α₁, α₂), with A'_{k₁+1} symmetric (twoDesc_key, twoDesc_key_classes; on a cycle, (2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ)(x_{k₂+1} + 1) = 2^{δ₂}E), holds with no ascending index. So m ≤ E(1, α₁, α₂) ≤ 5·2^{|Γ|−n} (twoDesc_adjacent), and the bound of the previous finding covers the case. It rests on the same two cited steps and nothing else. With δ₁ = 1 ≤ δ₂ the paper's own Δ_j also exists once n ≥ 3. The display of l.331 is unfinished: its i is not defined in this case, and its summand depends on k only through 3^{n−1−k}. It is not formalized.
syracuse.tex:308–334 — the key identity and the true two-term forms are not in the draft; the proofs here are new.
questions: OQ-63 (a): is Γ meant to be a cycle of positive integers? The statement is false over ℤ (the cycle of −17). Reading taken: none chosen. The ℤ statement is refuted, and the positive statement is derived from the two cited hypotheses.

Does 'Syracuse n-cycle' mean that n is the least period? With any period, the cycle (1) read as a 2-cycle refutes the statement for x > 0. Reading taken: least period, for the positive statement. The refutation over ℤ (−17) holds with n least, so it covers both readings.
l.308: '#𝒟_Γ = (k₁ + nℤ) ∪ (k₂ + nℤ)'. Reading taken: 𝒟_Γ = …. The equivalence with #(𝒟 ∩ ⟦1, n⟧) = 2 is proved, so this choice does not change the statement.

l.308 against l.310–322: which misprint, if any, does the author mean? One option: the positions of l.308 are as intended, and l.318, l.320 have α₁ and α₂ exchanged. The other: the displays of l.310–315 are as intended, the positions are swapped, and δ₁, δ₂ are exchanged at l.316. Reading taken: the positions of l.308. The true forms are stated there, and the printed displays and ∼_S forms are refuted under both readings.
OQ-43: is A_i the printed A_u^n or the product to n − 2 − k? Reading taken: both, everywhere. The ∼_S forms coincide.
OQ-68 (c): ∼_S. Reading taken: x ∼_S y iff x = s·y with s ∈ S, in ℚ (SEquiv). Each form is also an exact equality.
|Γ| and n/2 (l.323–324). Reading taken: |Γ| = p_n(x) = Σ_{t<n} a_t(x), and n/2 a real exponent.

The corollary to Matveev's theorem (l.326) and the GCD it bounds (OQ-68 (d)). Reading taken: its effective consequence for pairs (P, n), TwoDescMatveev B, at the exponent ε₀ and constant 2 proved here. The GCD is GCD(A'_i) = |2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ| (corGcdAlt, the OQ-43 reading). For the printed A_u^n, GCD(A_i) is even (strict Syracuse.gcd_Aun_ne_of_cycle) and is not bounded here.

kb_proposals: Two descending indices per period: run the step recursion two_pow_mul_AunAlt_succ once around the period in Z_u = A'_u + (2^P − 3ⁿ), where an ascending step reads 2Z_{u+1} = 3Z_u. One linear_combination with explicit coefficients gives D·(Z_c − 2^{r₁+1}E) = 0, and D odd cancels (Syracuse.twoDesc_key). Unlike DeltaAlt_eq_asc, it needs no ascending index.

Refute a ∼_S claim with a p-adic valuation at a prime p ∉ {2, 3}: padicValRat.mul, padicValRat.zpow, padicValRat.of_int, and v_p(2^u 3^v) = 0 (Syracuse.twoDesc_not_sEquiv, at p = 139). norm_num proves Fact (Nat.Prime 139) only with `import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum.Prime`.

A printed display whose integer exponents can be negative: define it in ℚ with zpow. norm_num evaluates it at literals (twoDescDisplayI); for general statements, rewrite each exponent to a ℕ-cast with omega, then zpow_natCast (twoDesc_displayI_eq).
A def using Finset.Icc on ℤ must be noncomputable (the order instance is), and `unfold` then `decide` still evaluates it (twoDescCount).

Representatives in ⟦1, n⟧: twoDesc_rep and twoDesc_rep_unique; no multiple of n lies strictly between 0 and n: twoDesc_not_mul. Pass (n := n) explicitly: it is not inferred from q * n = m with omega/linarith side goals.
`rw [← Finset.card_range n]` rewrites every n, the one inside `range n` included. Bound a product with Finset.prod_le_prod (g := fun _ => c), then prod_const and card_range.
p_n ≤ 2n on every cycle of ℤ (Syracuse.twoDesc_p_le): for x > 0 from the product form pow_p_mul_T_iterate_eq_prod, for x < 0 from two_pow_p_sub_three_pow_mul_pos.

Steiner.lean was neither read nor imported. The scaffold root SyracuseScaffold.lean was not touched. On the two hypotheses: TwoDescMatveev B mentions no cycle. It is true for some B by any lower bound of Baker type for 2^P − 3ⁿ; with theo:matveev as printed, 2^P/(eP)^d ≤ 2·2^{P(1−ε₀)} bounds P. TwoDescCheck B is believed true, since no positive cycle with two descending indices is known. Neither is proved here, so theo_syracuse_cycle_of_cited is worth what they are. Its analogue over ℤ fails for every B ≥ 11, by the cycle of −17 (p_7 = 11): the method of l.326, run over ℤ, finds −17 at the check. For T-syr-steiner, not formalized here: the proof of theo:steiner_2 at l.302 writes 2^{|Γ|−n} ≤ 2^{|Γ|(1−log₃2)}. That holds iff 3ⁿ ≥ 2^{|Γ|}, the same reversed direction as l.324, so it fails on every positive cycle.
